Build clique edges from pairwise comparison results

Source: R/comparison.R
comparison_to_edges.Rd

Converts output from summarize_comparison() into the edge format expected by find_cliques and classify_cliques. Renames columns, injects species identity, and computes per-pair effect sizes and classification.

Usage

comparison_to_edges(
  comparison,
  species1,
  species2,
  alternative = c("greater", "less"),
  alpha = 0.1,
  pval_combine = c("max", "min"),
  rho0 = NULL,
  p0 = NULL
)

Arguments

comparison

Data frame from summarize_comparison() (the $results element). Must contain columns gene1, gene2, hog, plus q-value and effect-size columns from both directions.

species1

Species abbreviation for gene1 genes (e.g., "BDIS").

species2

Species abbreviation for gene2 genes.

alternative

Which test direction to use for q-values and classification: "greater" (conservation, default) or "less" (divergence).

alpha

Significance threshold for the type column (default 0.1).

pval_combine

How the two directional q-values are combined into q_value: "max" (default; both directions must be significant – the reciprocal criterion of Netotea et al. (2014), the Max.p.val filter of the original ComPlEx) or "min" (permissive; a pair is called when either direction is significant, yielding a denser edge supply for find_cliques). A missing directional q-value is ignored in either case.

rho0

Reference fold enrichment for the power column: how many times more often than chance a conserved pair's partners are shared. NULL (default) takes, per direction, the median effect_size of the called pairs (about 2.5 on the Pooideae data); a single positive number fixes it for both directions.

p0

Rank-test frames only (from summarize_specificity(), carrying the AUROC grid): reference raw p for the power column, see summarize_specificity(). NULL (default) takes, per direction, the median raw p of the pairs called and significant in that direction.

Value

Data frame with columns:

gene1

Gene identifier (gene1)

gene2

Gene identifier (gene2)

hog

Ortholog group identifier

score

Evidence against chance in bits: -log2(p_value).

evalue

Expected number of pairs this significant by chance: n_tests * p_value.

species1

Species abbreviation for gene1 (species1)

species2

Species abbreviation for gene2 (species2)

p_value

The two directional p-values combined like pval_combine. Rank-test frames use the calibrated p (*.p.emp) when present. NA when the comparison has no p-value columns.

n_tests

Number of ortholog pairs tested, in the direction with more tests.

q_value

Maximum (or minimum, see pval_combine) of the two directional q-values

effect_size

Geometric mean of directional effect sizes

jaccard

Geometric mean of directional Jaccard indices (sqrt(species1.jaccard * species2.jaccard)). Range \([0, 1]\): 1 = identical neighborhoods, 0 = disjoint.

power

Detection power: the probability that the pair would have been called had its partners been shared at the reference fold enrichment rho0, given its neighbourhood sizes and the largest p-value called in each direction. Directions combine like pval_combine ("max": the weaker power). Power rises with degree: at typical enrichment a low-degree gene's shared partners amount to less than one, which no count test can call, so a non-significant low-power pair is absent evidence, not evidence of divergence. classify_gene_cliques and classify_cliques read it through min_power. NA for alternative = "less", when no pair is called in a direction, or when the comparison lacks the neighbourhood-size columns. For a rank-test frame (one carrying *.auroc.grid) it is the rank-test power instead, at reference rank p0 (see summarize_specificity()); there a direction with no call gives 0 rather than NA, so the classifiers read it as uninformative, not as a rejection.

type

"conserved" or "diverged" if q_value < alpha; "ns" otherwise

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
summary_AB <- summarize_comparison(comparison_AB)
edges_AB <- comparison_to_edges(summary_AB$results, "SP_A", "SP_B")

# Combine multiple species pairs for find_cliques()
edges <- rbind(edges_AB, edges_AC, edges_BC)
} # }
